name: Mudseam Acid-Walker's Layered Rig
description: A full-body survival layering system built from years of incremental replacement and desperate improvisation. The base is a long-sleeve thermal undershirt in faded ash-gray, once white, now permanently stained with rust runoff and machine oil, the cuffs fraying but tucked tight under self-repair tape at the wrists. Over it sits a quilted vest with salvaged thermal batting — the outer shell is acid-patched at both shoulders with mismatched swatches of rubberized tarp fabric, one olive-green and one gunmetal gray, bonded with industrial sealant that's gone slightly yellow at the edges. The outermost layer is a hip-length worker's jacket in faded black canvas, the back panel hand-stitched with a dense crosshatch of repair tape reinforcing a long acid-burn scar that runs from shoulder blade to hem. The collar has been modified with a fold-up neck guard, its inner lining a strip of reclaimed neoprene. Cargo pants in washed-out olive carry deep side pockets, one with a broken zipper replaced by a salvaged magnetic clasp, the knees double-layered with cut sections of conveyor belt rubber stitched on with heavy-gauge thread. Boots are resoled Shelf-cut work boots — the uppers are cracked leather, treated with a greasy waterproofing compound that gives them a dull, uneven sheen. The sole is a thick slab of reclaimed tire rubber, hand-cut and glued, with visible seam lines where the last resole job met the previous one. A wide utility belt in cracked synthetic leather carries two canteen pouches, a folded emergency rain sheet, and a multi-tool in a duct-tape sheath. The whole rig smells faintly of sealant, rain, and iron.
functionality: Full acid-rain resistance via layered patching and rubberized panels; thermal retention through quilted vest insert; deep cargo pockets for survival gear; fold-up neck guard; resoled boots with heavy-grip reclaimed rubber sole; magnetic clasp on primary pocket for one-handed access
what_it_says: This person has survived multiple acid seasons without new gear. Every repair is a record of a close call. The mismatched patches and industrial sealant communicate competence, not poverty — someone who knows exactly what the Shelf demands and has answered it over and over. No wasted material, no decorative choices. Pure accumulated survival intelligence.
worn_by: Shelf community elders who haven't moved up
manufacturer: Self-assembled; components sourced from Brineworks surplus, street market salvage, and personal fabrication
price_range: Φ 12–35 assembled; Φ 2–8 per component sourced individually
story_hooks: The acid-burn scar on the jacket's back is from a specific industrial incident three years ago — the same incident that killed two others. Someone recognizes it and knows what it means.
One of the cargo pockets contains something that was sewn shut — deliberately, carefully, with different thread than everything else. Whatever's inside has never been removed.
A CorpSec checkpoint officer recognizes the rubberized shoulder patches as material that was reported stolen from a Crucible subsidiary depot — and now wants to know how they got here.
